messages.subject: Field note: shallow moonquakes
messages.body: Apollo seismometers recorded shallow moonquakes that rang through the dry lunar crust for many minutes. Check whether a falling reading comes from a real leak or a shaken sensor before closing valves.

messages.subject: Independent gauge and hypothesis
messages.body: Kai's first guess is filed under hypothesis, not fact. Take the independent hand gauge to the three test taps along the falling line so we see which readings agree.

messages.subject: Filed under hypothesis
messages.body: Amara wrote my guess in the hypothesis column instead of crossing it out. I have the independent gauge ready for the three taps.

messages.subject: Three readings on the board
messages.body: All three tap readings are saved and only one branch fits every measurement. Come to the diagram and choose the smallest safe boundary that isolates the leak without starving the garden.

messages.subject: Keep the garden branch open
messages.body: The three saved readings clear the main garden line. If we pick the smallest boundary around the service branch, Alo and Tara keep their air and heat while we repair the joint.

messages.subject: Approved sequence and rollback
messages.body: Sequence approved and the rollback condition is written at the top of the card. If pressure drops on the habitat side during the clamp step, we back out immediately. Tools in hand.

messages.subject: Read-back before every turn
messages.body: We have the approved sequence and the rollback condition. Call each step out loud and wait for the read-back before seating the clamp.

messages.subject: Earth desk: boundary plan received
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. Your three-tap localization and boundary plan just arrived. Textbook isolation—your garden loop stays live while you clamp the service sleeve.

messages.subject: Leave the evidence visible
messages.body: The clamp is seated and the pressure line is holding flat. Leave the old fitting and its wear marks visible beside the clamp so we can run five timed checks before calling the room quiet.

messages.subject: Clamp seated
messages.body: Clamp seated, torque read back, and I did not cover the old seal mark. Amara wants the evidence visible for every single check.

messages.subject: Camera-only annex inspection granted
messages.body: Five post-repair checks are green. You have permission for a camera-only inspection of the service cover Kai saw move during the tremor. Do not unlatch the annex hatch until we review the feed.

messages.subject: The cover that moved
messages.body: I knew that service cover shifted when the floor shook! Camera and window only today—no heroics, just a clear look inside.

messages.subject: Viewing port closed, entry set for 8 May
messages.body: Viewing port shutter closed and the twenty-four-hour pressure hold is ticking. Scheduled annex entry is on the board for 8 May once every extended check passes.

messages.subject: Trays behind the glass
messages.body: Through the viewing port you can still see old growth trays laid out in rows. Waiting until 8 May is hard, but opening an unverified room would be worse.

messages.subject: Earth desk: 24-hour hold logged
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. Your clamp hold and camera inspection images are logged. Keep the viewing port closed overnight; you are cleared for the 8 May entry check.

messages.subject: Route sheet under a sealed cover
messages.body: Inside the annex we found a route sheet preserved under a sealed cover beside the unplanted trays. Bring it to the mission table so we can compare its bearings against our current station map.

messages.subject: Annex artifact logged: sealed route sheet
messages.body: Recovered from Annex Bay: one laminated ridge route sheet in a transparent protective sleeve, bearing hand-marked survey stations toward the southern cold-trap shelf.

messages.subject: Pod development 8 to 16 May
messages.body: The map notes are filed and eight days of dated pod development sit on the garden rack. Come check the siliques with me: a pod is ready on its own schedule, not because we are impatient.

messages.subject: Green pods on the stem
messages.body: From 8 May to 16 May the pods went from tiny threads to full green capsules. Mei says if I touch them before they dry, she will hide my favourite wrench.

messages.subject: Seed maturation and dry-down
messages.body: Harvesting brassica pods while they are still green and moist produces immature seeds that fail to store. Waiting through the five-day dry-down lets the embryo finish filling and cure safely.

messages.subject: Five-day dry-down vigil
messages.body: We leave the pods on the stem for the five-day dry-down: one photo a day in the exact same frame from 16 to 21 May. On the fifth day, bring the clean counting tray to the bench.

messages.subject: One photo a day
messages.body: Day four of the dry-down vigil. Everyone stops by the chamber window between watches to look at the same frame turning pale gold.

messages.subject: Annex route sheet and dry-down discipline
messages.body: I have your copy of the sealed route sheet and the daily pod photographs. Good patience holding off the harvest until the dry-down finishes tomorrow.

messages.subject: Forty-two seeds: 12 and 30
messages.body: Forty-two viable seeds counted on the bench: 12 for the active working stock and 30 divided 15 + 15 in the reserve compartments, plus one pressed petal in its sleeve. Let us choose where the petal rests.

messages.subject: 42 = 12 + 30 verified
messages.body: Founder harvest ledger signed: 42 total seeds, 12 allocated to working stock, 30 sealed in two reserve compartments of 15, and the pressed petal sleeve logged.

messages.subject: Where the petal can be seen
messages.body: The pressed petal is mounted where we can see it every shift, and the first working-stock seed is planted. On 31 May we say a proper farewell to Tara as her harvest joins the working stock.

messages.subject: Alo's petal in its sleeve
messages.body: Forty-two small clicks on the tray and one gold petal in its sleeve. The station feels less borrowed now.

messages.subject: Second hand light for guests
messages.body: July resupply unpacked. Kai hung a second hand light beside the locker 'for guests', handle out, and Amara showed him how she reads the independent gauge.

messages.subject: Green stems among purple on the October rack
messages.body: Five months of care are on the October rack: our saved May prediction beside the trays, a few green stems standing among the purple ones, and the cold-trap preparation list waiting on the map.

messages.subject: May prediction and the October map
messages.body: The Founder 30 reserve remains untouched at 15 + 15. Meet in the garden at 06:00 to compare our saved May prediction with the October rack before we brief the ridge traverse.

messages.subject: Earth desk: October traverse window
messages.body: Aurora, Earth desk. Five months of unbroken generational logs received. Your October 21 ridge lighting and horizon angles match the annex route sheet—proceed with the morning garden check and rover prep.
